titleEn: How to Hire a Licensed Renovation Contractor in Vancouver: What to Check in 2026
titleZh: 如何聘请持证装修承包商：温哥华2026年必查清单
contentEn:
Before signing any renovation contract in Vancouver, verify three things: the contractor's BC builder licence, their commercial general liability insurance, and their WorkSafeBC account status. These three documents protect you from the most common renovation disputes in Metro Vancouver. This guide explains exactly what to check, how to check it, and what to do if something does not add up.

Why Licensing Matters in Vancouver Renovations

BC's Home Inspector Licensing Act does not require a provincial licence for general renovation contractors, but the BC Residential Builder regime — administered by BC Housing — is mandatory for any contractor building new or performing major renovations that include structural, plumbing, or electrical work. A valid Residential Builder registration means the contractor has posted a $50,000 compliance bond and is subject to third-party dispute resolution through BC Housing's Homeowner Protection Office.

The City of Vancouver, City of Richmond, and most Metro Vancouver municipalities require a valid business licence before issuing renovation permits. An unlicensed contractor cannot pull permits in your name, which means any work they do may not be insurable or insurable under your home insurance policy.

The Three Documents Every Vancouver Homeowner Must Verify

1. BC Residential Builder Registration

Go to the BC Housing website (bchousing.gov.bc.ca) and use the Residential Builder search tool. Enter the company name or the owner's name. A registered builder will show an active registration number, the types of work they are registered for, and any current enforcement actions.

What to look for: Active status, registration number matching the contract, and no open enforcement files.

Ask the contractor for their BC Residential Builder registration number and verify it independently. Do not accept a copy of a licence as proof — look it up yourself.

2. Commercial General Liability Insurance ($5M minimum)

Ask for a certificate of insurance (COI) from the contractor's broker or insurer. The COI should show your property address as the job site, list you as the certificate holder, and show a minimum $5M limit for commercial general liability.

Call the broker's number on the COI to confirm the policy is active. Some contractors show outdated or cancelled policies. An active $5M CGL policy protects your home and your neighbours' properties if something goes wrong during construction — for example, water damage to a shared wall in a strata building.

3. WorkSafeBC Coverage Confirmation

Renovation workers injured on your property who are not covered by WorkSafeBC can make claims against your homeowner's insurance. This can result in higher premiums or a denied claim.

Ask the contractor for their WorkSafeBC account number and call WorkSafeBC directly at 1-888-494-9009 to confirm the account is active and the premiums are paid. Alternatively, use the WorkSafeBC employer search tool online.

Questions to Ask Before Signing Any Renovation Contract

Beyond the three documents above, these questions separate experienced contractors from amateurs:

  • How long have you been operating in Metro Vancouver? (Look for 5+ years)
  • Can I speak with three recent clients in my city? (A confident contractor provides these readily)
  • Who will be on site each day — your own crew or subcontractors?
  • Who is my main point of contact after signing?
  • What is your warranty policy and how long does it last?
  • Do you include project milestone schedules in the contract?

Red Flags: Signs of an Unlicensed or Unscrupulous Contractor

  • Asks for more than 30% of the total project cost as a deposit before any work begins
  • Cannot provide a BC Residential Builder registration number
  • Cannot provide a certificate of insurance listing your property address
  • Pressures you to sign quickly — "this price is only valid today"
  • Does not provide a written, signed contract before starting work
  • Asks you to obtain the building permit in your own name
  • Has no physical office or showroom — only a mobile phone number

What to Do If Something Goes Wrong

If a contractor performs unsatisfactory work or abandons the project, your recourse depends on which protections are in place. If the contractor is a BC-registered Residential Builder, file a complaint with the Homeowner Protection Office (housing.gov.bc.ca). If the contractor has an active CGL policy, contact their insurer to open a claim. If neither protection exists, you may need to pursue the matter through small claims court or the CRT (Civil Resolution Tribunal) for disputes under $5,000.

Before starting any project, confirm you have the contractor's BC Residential Builder number, a signed contract that includes a scope of work, a payment schedule tied to project milestones, and a warranty clause.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a handyman need a licence in Vancouver?

Minor cosmetic work — painting, drywall patching, replacing faucets — does not require a contractor licence in BC. However, any work involving structural changes, plumbing, or electrical must be performed by a licensed contractor or a homeowner acting as their own general contractor (which requires pulling permits in your own name). If the work requires a city building permit, a licensed contractor must do it.

What is the difference between a handyman and a renovation contractor?

A handyman typically handles minor repairs and cosmetic work without permits. A renovation contractor — for work requiring building, plumbing, or electrical permits — must hold a BC Residential Builder registration and be able to obtain permits in the city where the work takes place. Always confirm permit capability before signing a contract.

How much should I put as a deposit for a renovation in Vancouver?

15% to 20% at contract signing is standard practice in Metro Vancouver, tied to material orders. Do not pay more than 30% upfront before materials arrive on site. Avoid any contractor who asks for 50% or more as a deposit — this is a significant red flag.

What questions should I ask a renovation contractor in Vancouver?

Ask for their BC Residential Builder registration number and verify it on the BC Housing website. Ask for proof of $5M commercial general liability insurance naming you as certificate holder. Ask for a WorkSafeBC account confirmation. Ask for three references from recent projects in your city, and actually call them. Ask about their on-site supervision structure and who the main point of contact will be throughout the project.
contentZh:
在温哥华签署任何装修合同之前，请核实三件事：承包商的BC省建筑商执照、商业一般责任保险，以及WorkSafeBC账户状态。这三份文件保护您免受大温地区最常见的装修纠纷影响。本文详细说明要检查什么、如何检查，以及如果发现问题该怎么办。

为什么持证对温哥华装修很重要

BC省的房屋检查员执照法不要求一般装修承包商持有省级执照，但BC省住宅建筑商注册制度（由BC Housing管理）对任何从事新建或进行包含结构、管道或电气工程的主要装修工程的承包商是强制性的。有效的住宅建筑商注册意味着承包商已缴纳50,000加元的合规保证金，并受BC Housing房屋业主保护办公室的第三方争议解决机制的约束。

温哥华市、列治文市和大多数大温地区市政府在颁发装修许可证之前要求持有有效的营业执照。无执照承包商无法以您的名义申请许可证，这意味着他们进行的任何工程可能不在您的房屋保险承保范围内。

每位温哥华业主必须验证的三份文件

1. BC省住宅建筑商注册

访问BC Housing网站（bchousing.gov.bc.ca）并使用住宅建筑商搜索工具。输入公司名称或业主姓名。注册建筑商将显示有效注册号、注册工程类型以及任何当前的执法行动。

需要确认：有效状态、与合同匹配的注册号，以及无公开执法案件。

要求承包商提供其BC住宅建筑商注册号并自行独立核实。不要接受执照复印件作为证明——自己去查询。

2. 商业一般责任保险（最低$500万）

向承包商的经纪公司或保险公司索取保险证明（COI）。COI应显示您的房产地址为工地、列您为证书持有人，并显示商业一般责任险的最低$500万限额。

拨打COI上的经纪公司电话确认保单有效。一些承包商展示过期或取消的保单。有效的$500万CGL保单在施工期间发生问题时保护您的房屋和邻居的房产——例如，共管物业中共用墙的水损。

3. WorkSafeBC保险确认

如果装修工人在您的房产上受伤且不在WorkSafeBC承保范围内，他们可能向您的房屋保险提出索赔。这可能导致保费增加或索赔被拒绝。

要求承包商提供其WorkSafeBC账户号码，并直接拨打WorkSafeBC 1-888-494-9009确认账户有效且保费已缴。也可以在网上使用WorkSafeBC雇主搜索工具。

签署装修合同前要问的问题

除了上述三份文件外，以下问题区分有经验的承包商和业余人士：

  • 您在大温地区运营多长时间了？（寻找5年以上的）
  • 我能和您在我们城市的三个近期客户谈谈吗？（自信的承包商会 readily 提供这些）
  • 每天在现场的是您自己的团队还是分包商？
  • 签署后我的主要联系人是谁？
  • 您的保修政策是什么，保修期多长？
  • 您是否在合同中包含项目里程碑时间表？

计划在大温地区进行装修？获取Reno Stars的免费、无义务报价。Reno Stars是BC省持证住宅建筑商，持有$500万商业一般责任保险，并拥有活跃的WorkSafeBC保险。

危险信号：无证或不诚实承包商的迹象

  • 在任何工程开始前要求支付超过合同总金额30%作为定金
  • 无法提供BC住宅建筑商注册号
  • 无法提供列出您房产地址的保险证明
  • 催促您快速签署——"这个价格仅今天有效"
  • 在开始工程前不提供书面签名合同
  • 要求您以自己的名义获取建筑许可证
  • 没有实体办公室或陈列室——只有手机号码

如果出了问题该怎么办

如果承包商进行了令人不满意的工程或放弃项目，您的追索权取决于所到位的保护措施。如果承包商是BC注册住宅建筑商，请向房屋业主保护办公室（housing.gov.bc.ca）提交投诉。如果承包商有有效的CGL保单，请联系他们的保险公司提出索赔。如果两种保护都不存在，您可能需要通过小额索偿法庭或CRT（民事解决法庭，针对5,000加元以下的争议）追索。

在任何项目开始前，确认您有承包商的BC住宅建筑商号码、包含工程范围的签名合同、与项目里程碑挂钩的付款计划以及保修条款。

常见问题

在温哥华，散工需要执照吗？

轻微的美容工程——刷漆、修补干墙、更换龙头——在BC省不需要承包商执照。但是，任何涉及结构更改、管道或电气的工程必须由持证承包商执行，或由业主作为自己的总承包商（这需要以自己的名义申请许可证）执行。如果工程需要市建筑许可证，持证承包商必须执行。

散工和装修承包商有什么区别？

散工通常处理不需要许可证的轻微维修和美容工程。装修承包商——对于需要建筑、管道或电气许可证的工程——必须持有BC住宅建筑商注册，并能够在其施工所在城市获得许可证。在签署合同前始终确认许可能力。

在温哥华，装修定金应该付多少？

合同签订时支付15%至20%是标准做法，与材料订购挂钩。在材料到场之前不要支付超过30%。避免任何要求50%或更高定金的承包商——这是明显的危险信号。

我应该问装修承包商什么问题？

询问他们的BC住宅建筑商注册号并在BC Housing网站上核实。询问$500万商业一般责任保险的证明，将您列为证书持有人。询问WorkSafeBC账户确认。询问三个来自您所在城市近期项目的参考资料，并实际打电话给他们。询问他们的现场监管结构以及在整个项目期间的主要联系人是谁。

ko.title: 밴쿠버에서 면허 있는装修 계약자를 고용하는 방법：2026년 확인 사항
ko.content:
밴쿠버에서装修 계약을 체결하기 전에 3가지를 확인하세요: BC주 건설업자 면허, $500만 상업적 일반 책임 보험, WorkSafeBC 상태입니다. 이 가이드에서는 확인해야 할 내용, 확인 방법, 문제 발생 시 대처 방법을 설명합니다.

왜 면허가 중요합니까?

BC주 주거 건설업자 등록은 구조, 배관 또는 전기 작업이 포함된 주요改装에 필수입니다. 유효한 등록은 $50,000의合规 보증을 게시했음을 의미하며 BC Housing의 제3자 분쟁 해결 대상입니다.

확인해야 할 3가지 문서

1. BC주 주거 건설업자 등록 — BC Housing 웹사이트에서 확인. 2. 상업적 일반 책임 보험($500만 이상) — 보험 증명서를 취득하고 브로커에게 전화하여 유효성을 확인. 3. WorkSafeBC — 계좌 번호를 확인하고 직접 WorkSafeBC에 전화하여 확인.
